planting.note: Plant stem cuttings or container stock after last frost into average, well-drained, salt-tolerant soil in full sun to light shade; Beluntas tolerates brackish coastal conditions well.

directions: Plant in full sun to light shade in average, well-drained, salt-tolerant soil; Indian Camphorweed, known as beluntas or cúc tần in Vietnamese cooking, is a salt-tolerant evergreen coastal shrub reaching 3-10 feet, native to mangrove and tidal-flat habitats across Southeast Asia. Young leaves and shoot tips are eaten raw as a side dish with rice or added to salads and soups in Thailand, Java, and Vietnam. It propagates readily from stem cuttings and thrives in sunny, humid conditions with some salt or brackish tolerance, making it a good fit for Gulf Coast coastal gardens; it has no frost tolerance below roughly zone 9.

planting.note: Plant cuttings or container stock in spring against a trellis in full sun to bright filtered light; Skunk Vine is listed as invasive in parts of the US Southeast (notably Florida), so grow it in a contained bed or large pot rather than letting it spread into natural areas.

directions: Plant against a trellis in full sun to bright filtered light in average, well-drained soil; Skunk Vine is a fast-growing twining perennial vine with notably foetid-smelling leaves that are nonetheless a well-known Vietnamese wrap herb, lá mơ, traditionally paired with grilled meats and eaten raw with grated coconut and chili in Thailand and Vietnam. It dies back and resprouts from the roots in cooler zones, hardy to about zone 6a. It is federally flagged as invasive or noxious in parts of the US Southeast, including Florida, so grow it in a contained raised bed or large container rather than allowing it to spread into surrounding landscape or natural areas.

planting.note: Plant divisions after last frost into constantly moist to semi-aquatic soil in part shade to full sun; Basil-Leaf Limnophila needs a bog garden or pond-margin setting.

directions: Plant in part shade to full sun in constantly moist to semi-aquatic soil; Basil-Leaf Limnophila is a wetland and bog herb with bullate, basil-like, anise-scented leaves, closely related to the already-grown rice-paddy herb (Limnophila aromatica) but with a distinctly stronger anise note. It is used raw or cooked as a condiment across Thailand, Laos, Myanmar, and India. Grow it at a pond margin, rain garden, or bog planter where it can stay constantly wet; it is a true tropical with no frost tolerance.

planting.note: Plant stem cuttings in spring into average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Sabah Snake Grass propagates easily from cuttings.

directions: Plant in full sun to partial shade in average, well-drained soil; Sabah Snake Grass is an erect shrubby perennial reaching 3-10 feet, native to Southeast Asian forest edges and savanna. Its leaves are boiled fresh for a daily herbal tea in Malaysia and Vietnam, used medicinally more than as a cooking ingredient, functioning as a garden tea herb alongside other tisane plants. It propagates easily from stem cuttings and is strictly tropical to subtropical, with no frost tolerance, best grown in zones 10-11 or as a container plant brought indoors elsewhere.

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in spring into waterlogged, nutrient-rich soil in part shade; Prickly Lasia needs a bog garden or pond margin and has spiny petioles, so handle with gloves.

directions: Plant rhizome divisions in waterlogged, nutrient-rich soil in part shade, a bog garden or pond-margin setting; Prickly Lasia is a spiny-petioled aroid native to Thailand, Malaysia, India, and southwest China, grown for its young peeled leaf stalks and shoots, used as a curry-flavoring vegetable throughout mainland Southeast Asia and in Vietnamese regional cooking. Handle the spiny stalks with gloves when harvesting or dividing. It is a true tropical plant with no frost tolerance, needing constant wetness and warmth to thrive.

planting.note: Plant seed, root cuttings, or stem cuttings in spring into well-drained soil in full sun; Sambong loses aroma and vigor if grown in too much shade.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained soil; Sambong is a tall, camphor-scented perennial shrub reaching up to 13 feet, used across the Philippines and Vietnam primarily as a medicinal tea herb for traditional kidney-stone and respiratory remedies. It is frost-sensitive, dying back at temperatures just below freezing, and is best suited to zones 9a-11b. Propagate from seed, root division, or stem cuttings, and give it full sun, since the aromatic oils that give the plant its medicinal value diminish in shade.
